_comment: Home ports on the new company screen. great: 3 Scooters on the best nearby loop clear about $40,000 or more in their first 10 minutes from $150,000 (the starting money when the lists were made; it is now $500,000). harder: they clear about $10,000-$30,000, often by island hopping. excluded: not offered at all, because a Scooter has no port in range (isolated) or no profitable trade nearby (it loses money or barely breaks even); they are still normal ports in the game. Every other port is offered with a 'not recommended' note. Picked by simulating each HQ; recheck after changing markets.json, ship models or ports.

great.note: West African coffee and furniture with Banjul: the richest Scooter start, and the best gold run for the Laker.
The Gambia: coffee and furniture with Freetown; gold for the Laker.
Pacific Mexico: toys and coffee between Manzanillo and Baja California.
Manzanillo: toys and coffee up to Baja California.
Caribbean coffee sells high all the way up the US East Coast.
Coffee up from Miami; the whole East Coast within reach.
Coffee from Florida and the Bahamas sells well here.
East Coast coffee, then gold and iron ore up to Newfoundland.
Coffee to Florida, a short hop across the straits.
The Bahamas: coffee to Miami and Savannah.
The Atlantic end of the Panama Canal: coffee to Jamaica, ore from Ecuador.
The world's busiest port: coffee and toys down the coast to Quanzhou.
Coffee and toys up the China coast; Laker coal from Borneo.
China's toy factories on the doorstep, with coffee up the coast.
Southern Taiwan: across the strait to the Fujian coast.
Korea: across to Shanghai, then down the China coast.
The Mediterranean: toys and coffee to Malta, Sicily and Tunis.
North Africa: short runs to Malta and Rome.
Southern France: across the Tyrrhenian to Italy and Malta.
Egypt: the eastern Mediterranean between Israel and Turkey.
Haifa: coastal trade from Ashdod up to Mersin.
Ireland: toys and coffee across to Brittany and the Channel.
Portugal: runs down to the Strait of Gibraltar.
The Gulf: clothing between Dammam and Oman; oil and gas close by.
Chennai: across to Colombo in Sri Lanka.

harder.note: Island hopping: imports out to the outer islands, Kona coffee back; coal for Oahu. Thin margins, and the mainland is far away.
Hawaii's Big Island: Kona coffee to Honolulu, imports back.
American Samoa: imports across to Apia; Fiji's gold for the Laker.
Samoa: a very short hop to Pago Pago; gold from Fiji later.
Fiji: imports to Tonga, gold from the Vatukoula mine.
The Azores: good money out to the western islands, coal for Madeira, but a long way from anywhere.
Clothing from Osaka and coffee from Kobe; iron and coal for Nagoya's steelworks.
Tokyo Bay: coffee and clothing from Kansai, ore to Nagoya.
Osaka's clothing sells in Tokyo; ore runs along the coast.
Japan's coffee port: roasted beans for Tokyo.
Japan's steel and car city, between Tokyo and Osaka.
The Malacca Strait: steady coffee and toys with Penang; coal from Ho Chi Minh City.
Malaysia: the Malacca Strait between Penang and Singapore.
The top of the Malacca Strait, trading with Singapore.
Australia: toys up the coast to Brisbane; coal and iron for the Laker.
Queensland: down the coast to Sydney; coal and iron close by.
Europe's biggest port, but the margins are out west, from Le Havre to Dublin.
Belgium: the Channel run from Le Havre to Dublin.
The Thames: across the Channel to Le Havre and round to Dublin.
Colombian coffee for Jamaica; coal and iron through Panama later.
Jamaica: coffee with Colombia; ore through Panama later.
Colombia's Pacific port: up to Panama; gold and coal down to Peru.
The Philippines: runs to Cebu, and strong coal from Borneo.
The Bosphorus: the Black Sea to the Aegean.
The Baltic: furniture between Gdansk and Tallinn.
